## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dantikātherīgāthā* (Thig 3.4, corresponding to verses 48–50 of the collection) is a short poem in the *Therīgāthā* attributed to the nun (*bhikkhunī*) Dantikā [SuttaCentral; Collett 2014]. In these verses, Dantikā enters the depths of the forest for meditation and is inspired by the sight of a mahout subduing an elephant—the "untamed tamed"—to discipline, train, and order her own mind (*citta*) [Horner 1930].

Although Dantikā is not recorded in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*'s list of foremost nuns, she is preserved in the parallel list of outstanding *bhikkhunī*s in the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* [Collett 2014]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language textual parallels with a score of 10 or greater [DharmaNexus]. Text reuse within Pali literature is registered with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* across four passages (sharing 581 characters, primarily spanning segments §0.3–4.1 against commentary sections §711–718) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records sixteen translations across eleven languages, including modern English renderings by Bhikkhu Sujato and Ayya Soma [SuttaCentral].
